definition: To shut someone out of a group and refuse to accept them socially.
example: After he reported the cheating, a few teammates began to ostracize him in the locker room.
nuance: Ostracize suggests a group shutting someone out together, while shun can describe one person avoiding anyone or anything.
prompt: A new member joins a chess club whose regulars dislike his unusual openings.
options: The regulars began to ostracize the newcomer, leaving him without a partner every week.
The regulars chose to ostracize the newcomer by inviting him to every tournament dinner.
The club secretary helped ostracize the tournament schedule into neat rounds.
The regulars would ostracize his openings by writing a detailed analysis of each one.
reasons: The group pushes him out of its social circle, which is exactly what the verb describes.
Including someone in every gathering is the reverse of shutting him out.
This confuses the word with organize; a schedule cannot be socially excluded.
Studying or critiquing someone's moves is not the same as excluding the person.

practice.prompt: Residents of a quiet street react to a neighbor who painted her house bright purple.
options: The purple paint was so ostracize that drivers slowed down to stare at it.
One neighbor would ostracize her briefly by frowning once, then chatting as usual.
Some neighbors chose to ostracize her, no longer waving or inviting her to block parties.
Delighted by the color, the neighbors decided to ostracize her with a warm welcome basket.
reasons: This treats the verb as an adjective, probably mixing it up with ostentatious.
A single frown followed by normal friendliness does not push anyone out of a group.
Neighbors collectively cutting her off from social life fits the word.
A friendly gift signals acceptance, the opposite of rejection by a group.
